title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: RHONDA'S BALLOON
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Rhonda, a cereal factory boss in Battle Creek, Michigan.
She's afraid of ladders and elevators.
So of course, she won a hot air balloon ride.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PRIZE
segments.quote: What saves a man is to take a step. Then another step.
segments.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
lines: The radio station called. You won a sunrise flight!
At the field, her knees shook just looking at the basket.
Delbert, the seventy-year-old pilot, quoted a French flyer:
What saves a man is to take a step. Then another step.
So she lifted one leg over. Then the other. Then she held on tight.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: NO STEERING WHEEL
segments.quote: Some things are within our power while others are not.
segments.author: Epictetus
lines: Up they went, quiet as a cloud. Where's the steering wheel, Rhonda asked.
There isn't one. The wind steers. I just pick up or down.
Rhonda nearly fainted. Delbert quoted Epictetus, a Greek teacher:
Some things are within our power while others are not.
So she let the wind drive, and finally looked down. Beautiful.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE CHASE CREW
segments.quote: Nothing ever comes to one, that is worth having, except as a result of hard work.
segments.author: Booker T. Washington
lines: Rhonda wanted more. So she joined Delbert's chase crew.
Four a.m., folding a balloon the size of a house.
Her back ached. Delbert quoted Booker T. Washington:
Nothing ever comes to one, that is worth having, except as a result of hard work.
By August, she folded that balloon faster than Delbert.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: GROUNDED
segments.author: Ernest Shackleton
lines: Then she went for her own pilot's license. She told only her cat.
But Michigan weather said no. Seven Saturdays in a row, too windy to fly.
She wanted to quit. Delbert quoted the polar explorer Ernest Shackleton:
Optimism is true moral courage.
So every grounded Saturday, she showed up anyway, with donuts.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE TEST
segments.quote: Victory awaits him who has everything in order — luck, people call it.
segments.author: Roald Amundsen
lines: She took the written test, and failed. By two weather questions.
She blamed bad luck. Delbert quoted the explorer Roald Amundsen:
Victory awaits him who has everything in order — luck, people call it.
So she made checklists, and studied weather maps at lunch.
Next test? Ninety-four percent.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE VIEW
segments.quote: The world will never starve for want of wonders; but only for want of wonder.
segments.author: G. K. Chesterton
lines: One clear October morning, Rhonda flew solo over Battle Creek.
There was her factory, her bowling alley, her own little roof.
She'd never really looked. She thought of the English writer G. K. Chesterton:
The world will never starve for want of wonders; but only for want of wonder.
She waved. Her sister waved back with a dish towel.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Take a step. Let the wind steer. Work hard. Stay hopeful. Get ready. Look again.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Take one step. Let the wind steer. Work hard. Stay hopeful. Get ready. And look again.
I went up in a balloon once. The pilot looked at me and said, we're gonna need more hot air.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
